<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par87 />{{GHGheb|text=תְּהִלִּים}}, as in the headings of the printed editions, as well as {{GHGheb|text=סֵ֫פֶר תְּהִלּוֹת|translate=the Book of Psalms}}); {{GHGheb|text=אִגֶּ֫רֶת|translate=a letter}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=אִגְּרוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵר|translate=a well}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵרוֹת}}. Feminines in {{GHGheb|text=־ִית}} form their plural in {{GHGheb|text=־ִיּוֹת}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִצְרִית|translate=an Egyptian woman}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מִצְרִיּוֹת}}; and those in {{GHGheb|text=וּת}} either make {{GHGheb|text=־ֻיּוֹת}}, as {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכוּת|translate=kingdom}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=מַלְכֻיּוֹת}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=8|verse=22}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=חֲנֻיּוֹת|translate=cells}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=16}}), or are inflected like {{GHGheb|text=עֵֽדְוֹת|translate=testimonies}} (pronounced ''ʿēdh<sup>e</sup>wôth'' for ''ʿēdhŭwôth'').

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|k}}
It is only from a mistake or disregard of these feminine endings {{GHGheb|text=־וּת}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ִית}} that some words ending with them form their plural by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} or {{GHGheb|text=־וֹת}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חֲנִית|translate=spear}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=חֲנִיתִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=חֲנִיתוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=זְנוּת|translate=whoredom}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=זְנוּתִים}} (by the side of {{GHGheb|text=זְנוּנִים}}); {{GHGheb|text=אַלְמְנוּתִים|translate=widowhood}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁחִיתוֹת|translate=pits}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּסָתוֹת|translate=amulets}} (if connected with Assyr. ''kâsu'', ''to bind''), &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|l}}
The termination -''ôth'' stands primarily for -''âth'' (which is the form it has in Arab., Eth., in the ''constr. st''. of Western Aramaic, in Eastern Syriac, and also in Assyrian; on the change of ''â'' into an obscure ''ô'', see {{GHGpar|9|q}}). On the other hand, it is doubtful whether this ''âth'' is to be regarded as a lengthened and stronger form of the singular fem. ending ''ăth'' (cf. {{GHGpar|80|b}}).

How the changeable vowels of a noun are shortened or become {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} in consequence of the addition of the plural endings is explained in §§ 92–5.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|m}}
'''3.''' Words which in the singular are used both as masculine and feminine ({{GHGpar|122|d}}), often have in the plural parallel forms with the masculine and feminine terminations, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עָב|translate=cloud}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=עָבִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=עָבוֹת}}; and each form may be treated either as masculine or feminine, according to the usage of the particular word.—But even those words, of which the gender is invariable, sometimes have both plural forms, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹר}} masc. ''a generation'', plur. {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹרִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹרוֹת}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה}} fem. ''a year'', plur. {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנוֹת}} (see the Rem.). In these words the gender of both plural forms remains the same as in the singular, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֲרִי}} masc. ''a lion'', plur. {{GHGheb|text=אֲרָיוֹת}} masc., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zp|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹרוֹת}} masc., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=16}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|n}}
Sometimes usage makes a distinction between the two plural forms of the same word. Thus, {{GHGheb|text=יָמִים|translate=days}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנִים|translate=years}} are the usual, but {{GHGheb|text=יָמוֹת}} (only twice, in the ''constr. st''. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=15}}) and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנוֹת}} (also only in the ''constr. st''. and before suffixes) are rarer poetic forms.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|o}}
A difference of meaning appears in several names of members of the body, the dual (see § 88) denoting the living members themselves, while the plur. in {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} expresses something like them, but without life ({{GHGpar|122|u}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָדַ֫יִם|translate=hands}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָדוֹת|translate=artificial hands}}, also e.g. the ''arms'' of a throne; {{GHGheb|text=כַּפַּ֫יִם|translate=hands}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּפּוֹת|translate=handles}} (Lat. ''manubria''); {{GHGheb|text=פַּ֫עַם|translate=foot}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּעָמוֹת|translate=artificial feet}} (of the ark), {{GHGheb|text=קַרְנַ֫יִם|translate=horns}}, {{GHGheb|text=קְרָנוֹת|translate=horns}} (of the altar); {{GHGheb|text=עֵינַ֫יִם|translate=eyes}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֲיָנוֹת|translate=fountains}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=אֲרָיִים|translate=lions}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲרָיוֹת}} the ''figures of lions'' on Solomon’s throne, {{GHGheb|text=תָּמָר|translate=palm}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽמֹרָה|translate=a palm-like column}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽמֹרִים}} and {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽמֹרוֹת}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|p}}
'''4.''' A considerable number of masculines form their plural in {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}}, while many feminines have a plural in {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}}. The gender of the singular, however, is as a rule retained in the plural.<section end=par87 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
